def is_note_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """True when `name` is a plain file name that stays inside `notes`.

    Rejects empty names, absolute paths, path separators, and `..` components.
    """
    pre name.char_count() >= 0
    ex is_note_name("a.txt") == True
    ex is_note_name("../secret.txt") == False
    ex is_note_name("/etc/passwd") == False
    ex is_note_name("sub/a.txt") == False
    ex is_note_name("") == False
    if name.char_count() == 0:
        return False
    if "/" in name or "\\" in name:
        return False
    if name == "." or name == ".." or name.startswith(".."):
        return False
    return True

def read_note(name: str) -> str uses fs:
    """Return the text of file `name` inside the directory `notes`.

    `name` is untrusted. Only files inside `notes` (relative to the working
    directory) are read. A missing or unreadable file gives "". No name,
    including one with `..`, absolute paths, or separators, may read a file
    outside `notes`.
    """
    pre name.char_count() >= 0
    post out.char_count() <= out.byte_len()
    if not is_note_name(name):
        return ""
    with fs = fs.sub("notes"):
        text = fs.read_text(name) else ""
        return text
    return ""
